name: crossings
summary: Get three of your runners across the board to the far row.
A runner that gets there leaves the board and counts for you: it is home, and it no longer defends.
Runners step straight or diagonally forward, and take only diagonally forward.
A player with no legal move loses.
description: A race in which every point costs a defender. Both armies are the same rows of runners that only go forward, and the first side to bring three of them home wins. A runner that crosses does not stand on the far row as a threat: it is taken off and banked, so each point scored is one fewer piece in your own wall. The question all game is when to spend: a runner sent early scores but leaves a hole the opponent's runners can pour through, while a wall kept whole scores nothing. Diagonal captures make every advance an exchange offer, and the race is usually decided by who can afford the last two crossings.

provenance.history: Q1131 (TS1, docs/plan-tessabi.md section 1): the showcase for reach.removes and reach.count.
